root_cause.text: In x86 UV hub initialization, uv_system_init_hub() used uv_blade_to_node(bid) directly as the NUMA node for kzalloc_node(), so deconfigured sockets mapped to SOCK_EMPTY (0xffff) were treated as a valid node ID and triggered a panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check around `nid = uv_blade_to_node(bid); if (nid == SOCK_EMPTY) nid = NUMA_NO_NODE;` before calling `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, nid)`, and both the CVE and commit message state that deconfigured sockets are mapped to `SOCK_EMPTY` and this “causes a panic while allocating UV hub info structures.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a check around `nid = uv_blade_to_node(bid); if (nid == SOCK_EMPTY) nid = NUMA_NO_NODE;` before calling `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, nid)`, and both the CVE and commit message state that deconfigured sockets are mapped to `SOCK_EMPTY` and this “causes a panic while allocating UV hub info structures.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle deconfigured sockets by mapping `SOCK_EMPTY` to `NUMA_NO_NODE` before per-hub allocation so `kzalloc_node()` uses a valid NUMA node.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a conditional expression assigning `new_hub` with an explicit `if/else` block: for `bid == 0` it still uses `&uv_hub_info_node0`, and for other blades it now stores `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` in a local `nid`, checks whether `nid == SOCK_EMPTY`, substitutes `NUMA_NO_NODE` in that case, and then calls `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, nid)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, allocation for nonzero blade IDs no longer passes the `SOCK_EMPTY` sentinel as a NUMA node to `kzalloc_node`; instead, deconfigured sockets fall back to `NUMA_NO_NODE`, ensuring allocation occurs on a valid node and preventing invalid-node allocation behavior or failures for empty/deconfigured sockets.

grouping_result.intent: Handle deconfigured sockets by mapping `SOCK_EMPTY` to `NUMA_NO_NODE` before per-hub allocation so `kzalloc_node()` uses a valid NUMA node.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by detecting deconfigured sockets (`SOCK_EMPTY`) and converting them to `NUMA_NO_NODE` before calling `kzalloc_node()`, preventing use of the invalid node ID `0xffff`.

candidates.rationale: This allocation passes uv_blade_to_node(bid) directly as the NUMA node. When a deconfigured socket maps to SOCK_EMPTY (0xffff), that invalid value is used as a node ID for kzalloc_node(), leading to the panic described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly uses uv_blade_to_node(bid) as the NUMA node for kzalloc_node(). When a deconfigured socket causes uv_blade_to_node(bid) to return SOCK_EMPTY (0xffff), that invalid value is passed as a node ID, triggering the panic described in the root cause.

Sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) invalidates previous assumptions of a 1:1
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8a50c58519271dd24ba760bb282875f6ad66ee71
Author: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Date:   Fri May 19 14:07:50 2023 -0500

    x86/platform/uv: UV support for sub-NUMA clustering
    
    Sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) invalidates previous assumptions of a 1:1
    relationship between blades, sockets, and nodes.  Fix these
    assumptions and build tables correctly when SNC is enabled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
    Signed-off-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full relevant allocation logic inside `uv_system_init_hub()`. The root cause is allocating hub info with `kzalloc_node()` using `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` directly, which can return `SOCK_EMPTY (0xffff)` for deconfigured sockets. That exact construct is present here: `new_hub = (bid == 0) ?  &uv_hub_info_node0 : kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, uv_blade_to_node(bid));`. There is no validation that `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` is a real NUMA node, no check against `SOCK_EMPTY`, and no fallback to a safe node before calling `kzalloc_node()`. The later checks only verify allocation success (`if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!new_hub))`) and do not prevent passing an invalid node ID into `kzalloc_node()`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet in this function.
